sources.entry: 📖 Clean Architecture, Robert C. Martin. Uncle Bob proposes an architecture that leverages the Single Responsibility Principle to its fullest. A great way to start a new codebase. Also checkout the clean architecture cheatsheet and this article.

summary.title: The Clean Architecture
summary.one_liner: Robert C. Martin's concentric-circle architecture separates business rules from UI, database and frameworks by enforcing the Dependency Rule, where source code dependencies only point inward.
takeaways: Source code dependencies must point inward: inner circles must never name anything declared in outer circles.
Layers are Entities (enterprise business rules), Use Cases (application rules), Interface Adapters (controllers, presenters, gateways) and Frameworks and Drivers (DB, web, UI).
Dependency Inversion lets inner layers call outward through interfaces that outer layers implement, so flow of control can cross boundaries while dependencies still point inward.
Only simple, isolated data structures should cross boundaries, not database rows or framework-generated formats.
Business rules become testable without UI, database or web server, and the database, UI and frameworks can be swapped with little effort.
summary.summary: The article presents a unified architecture that integrates Hexagonal, Onion, DCI, BCE and Screaming Architecture, all of which separate concerns into layers with business rules at the center. It is illustrated with a diagram of concentric circles and explains the Dependency Rule, then describes each layer: Entities, Use Cases, Interface Adapters, and Frameworks and Drivers. It shows how control flow crosses boundaries using interfaces such as a Use Case Output Port implemented by a presenter. It closes by noting the number of circles is schematic and that simple data structures should cross boundaries.
